stem:
Neutrase® is an enzyme that is used to hydrolyse proteins in solution. When the enzyme is mixed with a $2\%$ protein solution the reaction mixture changes from white to colourless.

A student carried out an experiment to find the effect of copper sulfate and potassium sulfate on the activity of Neutrase®.

The student made four reaction mixtures in test-tubes A to D. Test-tubes A to C contained equal volumes of protein solution and $0.1\text{cm}^3$ of solutions of copper sulfate or potassium sulfate. Test-tube D contained the same volume of protein solution and $0.1\text{cm}^3$ of water.

$0.5\text{cm}^3$ of a $1\%$ Neutrase® solution was added to test-tube A and immediately placed into a colorimeter. The colorimeter was used to measure the intensity of light that is absorbed by the solution (absorbance) over 100 seconds. The procedure was repeated with the other reaction mixtures, B, C and D.

The results are shown in Fig. 3.1.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Suggest and explain why measuring the absorbance of the reaction mixture over $100\text{ s}$ is a suitable method for determining the activity of Neutrase®.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
With reference to Fig. 3.1:

• describe the effects of copper sulfate solution and potassium sulfate solution on the activity of Neutrase®
• suggest explanations for the effects that you have described.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Neutrase® can be immobilised in alginate. Immobilised Neutrase® is used in the food industry to produce foods with high nutritional content.

Explain the advantages of using immobilised enzymes, such as Neutrase®, compared with using the same enzymes free in solution.
